1.stem_plain: __________ I was exhausted after a long day at school, I stayed up late to complete the project.

2.stem_plain: When I was at the shopping centre yesterday, I saw the police __________ after a shoplifter.

3.stem_plain: "You won't tell anyone about my mistake, __________?" Alfred asked worriedly.

4.stem_plain: If we __________ our revisions earlier, we would have done better in the exams.

5.stem_plain: All the members of George's family __________ excited about going to the cinema after the easing of the Covid-19 safety management measures next month.

6.stem_plain: "You __________ television since nine this morning. You should stop now and read a book instead," Mr. Lee told his daughter.

7.stem_plain: "I will be taking the end-of-year examinations __________ a week's time," said Agnes confidently.

8.stem_plain: "Let's walk more quickly or we'll miss our connecting flight to Hong Kong. There isn't __________ time to waste," Mrs Tan told her children.

9.stem_plain: Based on the laws in Singapore, you __________ have a license issued by the Traffic Police before you are allowed to drive a car.

10.stem_plain: My teacher praised my friends and __________ for helping the younger students.

1.note: 前半句“我很累”与后半句“我熬夜完成项目”在逻辑上存在让步、转折关系（虽然……但是），使用连词 Although 最符合语境。
1.concept: 让步状语从句 — Concession Clauses — Although
1.zh: 虽然在学校度过了漫长的一天后我很累，但我还是熬夜完成了这个项目。

2.note: 感官动词的固定搭配：see somebody doing something 强调看到某人正在进行某个动作。此处指看到警察正在追捕扒手。
2.concept: 感官动词固定搭配 — Verbs of Perception — see sb doing sth
2.zh: 昨天我在购物中心时，看到警察正在追捕一个扒手。

3.note: 反义疑问句遵循“前否后肯”原则。陈述部分含有否定词 won't（will not），因此疑问尾句必须使用肯定形式 will you。
3.concept: 反义疑问句 — Question Tags — Negative Statement to Positive Tag
3.zh: “你不会把我的错误告诉任何人的，对吗？”阿尔弗雷德担忧地问。

4.note: 本句是对过去发生事情的虚拟假设（第三类条件句）。主句使用了 “would have done”，则 if 条件句中必须使用过去完成时（had + 过去分词）had begun。
4.concept: 虚拟语气（与过去事实相反）— Conditional Type 3 — Past Unreal Conditional
4.zh: 如果我们早点开始复习，我们在考试中就会考得更好。

5.note: 主语为 “All the members of George's family”，核心词是复数名词 members，故谓语动词需用复数。时间状语为 “next month”（下个月），表明该时间还未发生，且这里强调未来的状态，使用一般现在时复数 are 表达安排或既定未来的状态最为恰当。
5.concept: 主谓一致与时态 — Subject-Verb Agreement & Future/Present Context
5.zh: 在下个月放宽 Covid-19 安全管理措施后，乔治家的所有成员都对去电影院感到很兴奋。

6.note: 时间状语 “since nine this morning” 意为“从今天早上九点开始”，与之搭配的动作 “watch” 持续到现在，并对现在产生影响，应当使用现在完成进行时 have been watching。
6.concept: 现在完成进行时 — Present Perfect Continuous Tense — since clauses
6.zh: “你从今天早上九点起就一直在看电视。你现在应该停下来，去读本书。”李先生对他的女儿说。

7.note: 固定搭配 “in a week's time” 或 “in [时间段] time”，表示“在……时间之后”，常用于将来时态的句子中。
7.concept: 时间介词短语 — Prepositions of Time — in ... time
7.zh: “我将在一周后参加期末考试，”艾格尼丝自信地说。

8.note: 不可数名词 “time” 用于否定句 “there isn't...” 时，表示“没有很多时间”，应当用 much 修饰。few 和 many 只能修饰可数名词复数。
8.concept: 限定词与名词修饰 — Quantifiers — much with uncountable nouns
8.zh: “我们走快点，否则就会错过飞往香港的衔接航班了。没有多少时间可以浪费了，”谭夫人对他的孩子们说。

9.note: 根据前置语境 “Based on the laws in Singapore”（根据新加坡法律），说明后文是在阐述一项法律层面的强制性义务，因此应使用表“必须、强制”的情态动词 must。
9.concept: 情态动词表义务 — Modal Verbs — must for obligation
9.zh: 根据新加坡法律，你必须在获得交通警察颁发的驾照后才被允许开车。

10.note: 及物动词 “praised” 后面需要接宾语。在这个并列宾语结构中，“my friends and __________” 整体充当宾语，因此空格处需填入人称代词的宾格形式 me。
10.concept: 代词的格 — Pronoun Case — Object Pronouns in Compound Objects
10.zh: 我的老师表扬了我的朋友们和我，因为我们帮助了年幼的学生。

11.stem_plain: Mrs Tan __________ when her son, Cecil, lost his water bottle for the third time this year.

12.stem_plain: The pandemic has caused many companies to __________ on their spending during the lockdown.

13.stem_plain: The school informed the students that their graduation certificates would be __________ in an envelope with a congratulatory letter next week.

14.stem_plain: Please make sure that you email the submission to the school immediately. It is __________.

15.stem_plain: The earthquake hit the city and its habitants without __________.

11.zh: 当陈太太的儿子塞西尔今年第三次丢掉水壶时，她气炸了。
11.note: hit the roof 是一个固定习语，意为“勃然大怒、气炸了”，符合母亲因儿子屡次丢东西而极度愤怒的语境。
11.concept: 习语辨析与语境匹配 — Idiomatic Expressions — hit the roof

choices.zh: 勃然大怒，大发雷霆，气炸了（习语，形容人因某事突然变得极其愤怒，大声斥责）
choices.eg: My father will **hit the roof** if he finds out that I have scratched his brand new car.

choices.zh: 咬紧牙关，硬着头皮，咬牙挺住（习语，指面对无法逃避的痛苦或艰难处境时，下定决心去面对）
choices.eg: She finally **bit the bullet** and went to the dentist to get her decayed tooth extracted.

choices.zh: 逼她表态，迫使她提前行动（习语，指由于外界某种压力或事态发展，迫使某人做出了原本不想做或不想这么早做的事）
choices.eg: The sudden leak of the corporate secret **forced her hand** to announce the product launch early.

choices.zh: 说话拐弯抹角，绕圈子，不切入正题（习语，指说话时故意回避核心问题，不直接表明意图）
choices.eg: Stop **beating around the bush** and tell me exactly how much money you need to borrow.

12.zh: 在封锁期间，这场流行病导致许多公司缩减了开支。
12.note: cut back on spending 为固定短语搭配，意为“削减、缩减（开支、预算等）”，符合公司在经济困难时期开源节流的语境。
12.concept: 短语动词辨析与固定搭配 — Vocabulary — Phrasal Verbs with 'cut'

choices.zh: 切碎，剪碎；（在公共场所）胡闹（动词短语，指用刀或剪刀把物体分成许多小块）
choices.eg: The mother carefully **cut up** the juicy steak into small pieces for her toddler.

choices.zh: 切断，断绝，使隔绝（动词短语，指中断电力、水源、电话等供应，或切断两地之间的交通往来）
choices.eg: The electricity supply to the building was **cut off** because the bill had not been paid.

choices.zh: 裁剪出；停止，戒掉（动词短语，指从报刊等纸张上剪下特定图形，或指停止某种不健康的行为、饮食）
choices.eg: The doctor advised the patient to **cut out** sugary snacks from his daily diet.

choices.zh: 削减，缩减，减少（动词短语，后常接 on，指为了省钱或控制总量而减少某物的消耗或花费）
choices.eg: Due to the economic recession, the family had to **cut back** on luxury holidays and dining out.

13.zh: 学校通知学生，他们的毕业证书下周将和一封祝贺信一起随信封附上。
13.note: be enclosed in an envelope 意为“随信封附上/装在信封内”，属于信件往来或正式公文寄送时的标准词汇搭配。
13.concept: 动词辨析与书信场景搭配 — Vocabulary — Verbs

choices.zh: 注册，招收，入学（动词，指正式登记加入学校、课程或某个官方组织团体）
choices.eg: My parents **enrolled** me in a reputable swimming academy during the school holidays.

choices.zh: 把……装入箱内，把……包住（动词，指用坚固的外壳或保护套将某件珍贵、易碎的物品紧紧包裹起来）
choices.eg: The museum's ancient gold coins were securely **encased** in thick bulletproof glass cases.

choices.zh: 随信附上，附入，把……围起来（动词，指在信件、包裹里顺便放入其他文件，或用围栏将一片土地封闭）
choices.eg: Please find **enclosed** a copy of my official resume for your corporate reference.

choices.zh: 诱骗，使落入陷阱（动词，常指设计圈套欺骗某人或动物，使其陷入无法逃脱的困境或犯错）
choices.eg: The small woodland animals were **entrapped** by the heavy nets laid out by the illegal poachers.

14.zh: 请务必立即将提交的文件发邮件给学校。这件事情很紧急。
14.note: 由前半句的 immediately（立即、马上）可知，这件事情的时效性极强，属于“紧急的、十万火急的”，故选 urgent。
14.concept: 形容词辨析与逻辑关联 — Vocabulary — Adjectives

choices.zh: 轻快的，生机勃勃的，寒冷而清爽的（形容词，形容走路步伐迅速轻快，或生意兴隆、天气凉爽）
choices.eg: The doctor recommended taking a **brisk** thirty-minute walk every single morning.

choices.zh: 草率的，仓促的，轻率的（形容词，常带有贬义，指由于时间不够或没过脑子，做出的决定过于急忙和粗心）
choices.eg: She later regretted her **hasty** decision to resign from the firm without finding a backup.

choices.zh: 紧急的，急迫的，迫切的（形容词，指某项任务或情况非常危急，必须立刻予以关注和处理，不容拖延）
choices.eg: The surgeon was called to the operating theatre to handle an **urgent** emergency case.

choices.zh: 突然的，唐突的，生硬的（形容词，指某种变化、转折在毫无预兆的情况下发生，或形容人说话粗鲁不客气）
choices.eg: The interview came to an **abrupt** end when the candidate suddenly stood up and walked away.

15.zh: 地震在毫无预兆的情况下袭击了这座城市及其居民。
15.note: without warning 是固定搭配，意为“毫无预兆地、在没有得到任何警告/前兆的情况下”，符合地震这类自然灾害突然爆发的特点。
15.concept: 名词辨析与固定搭配 — Vocabulary — Collocations with 'without'

choices.zh: 通知，布告，注意（名词，指书面或口头的正式通知、告示，或被公众注意到的状态）
choices.eg: The landlord gave us a one-month **notice** before raising the monthly house rent.

choices.zh: 警告，预兆，前兆（名词，指对即将发生的危险、惩罚或糟糕状况提前发出的信号、口头警告）
choices.eg: The severe storm struck the coastal fishing village without any prior **warning**.

choices.zh: 犹豫，踌躇（名词，指在做某事、说话或决定之前，因不确定或害怕而产生的短暂迟疑）
choices.eg: When she saw the toddler falling into the pool, she jumped in without a moment's **hesitation**.

choices.zh: 打断，中断，干扰（名词，指某项活动、进程或讲话被外界因素强行停止、打扰的状态）
choices.eg: The teacher requested the children to read their books quietly without any **interruption**.

16.note: 词义辨析 — 习语“get their creative juices flowing”意为使文思泉涌、激发创造力或灵感，与“think ingeniously（别出心裁地、充满创意地思考）”最为贴合。

choices.zh: 能赚钱地/划算地思考
choices.eg: He spent hours figuring out how to think profitably in business.

choices.zh: 充满创意地/别出心裁地思考
choices.eg: The team needs to think ingeniously to design a completely unique logo.

choices.zh: 富有成效地思考
choices.eg: A morning walk helps her clear her mind and think productively.

choices.zh: 建设性地思考
choices.eg: Instead of arguing, we should focus on trying to think constructively.

17.note: 词义辨析 — 在摄影语境下，“capture these beautiful images”意为抓拍、拍摄下这些画面，与动词“take（拍摄、捕捉画面）”最为对应。

choices.zh: 拍摄，抓拍，捕捉（照片/画面）
choices.eg: The photographer stepped forward to take a quick photo of the bird.

choices.zh: 钩住，吸引住
choices.eg: The opening scene of the exciting movie managed to hook the audience.

choices.zh: 抓住，接住
choices.eg: The little boy managed to catch the ball with one hand.

choices.zh: 抓住，夺取（机会/控制权）
choices.eg: You should seize the opportunity to study overseas.

18.note: 词义辨析 — “very good knowledge and experience”指在某种技能上拥有极高的熟练度、精通程度，与名词“the proficiency（熟练、精通）”意思最接近。

choices.zh: 敏捷度，灵活性
choices.eg: The gymnasts performed the complex moves with extreme agility.

choices.zh: 天资，天赋（常接for）
choices.eg: From a very young age, she showed a natural aptitude for music.

choices.zh: 潜力，潜能
choices.eg: The coach believes that the young athlete has great potential.

choices.zh: 熟练度，精通，通晓
choices.eg: The job description requires high proficiency in data processing software.

19.note: 词义辨析 — “appetising”形容食物看起来美味可口、引人食欲的，与“delectable（美味的、怡人的）”意思完全一致。

choices.zh: 可食用的（指能吃、无毒）
choices.eg: These wild mushrooms look colorful but they are completely edible.

choices.zh: 讨人喜欢的，可爱的
choices.eg: The main character in the story is friendly and very likeable.

choices.zh: 令人愉快的，欣然同意的
choices.eg: We spent a highly agreeable afternoon strolling near the river bank.

choices.zh: 美味可口的，引人食欲的
choices.eg: The local bakery makes delectable pies filled with fresh berries.

20.note: 词义辨析 — “typically”指通常情况下、一般而言，与副词“commonly（通常、普遍）”意思相符。

choices.zh: 通常地，普遍地，一般情况下
choices.eg: This specific plant is commonly found in tropical rain forests.

choices.zh: 连续不断地，频繁地
choices.eg: The old machine continually breaks down and requires repairs.

choices.zh: 坚持不懈地，固执地
choices.eg: She persistently pursued her academic dream despite all challenges.

choices.zh: 偶尔，有时
choices.eg: They occasionally go to the theatre to watch a classical drama.

cloze: Have you ever seen a photograph of a steak, salad or slice of strawberry shortcake that made your mouth water? Images like these are the creations of skilled food photographers with an eye for details. These artists [Q16(get their creative juices flowing)] to make their audience crave a dish without the help of the food's actual presence, taste, aroma and texture. Food photographers work to create and [Q17(capture)] these beautiful and enticing images of food for magazines, menus, cookbooks and other types of media. They must have [Q18(very good knowledge and experience)] in using a digital camera and related technologies.

They work with food stylists to make the food look as [Q19(appetising)] and appealing as possible. There are approximately 1,000 photographers employed in Singapore. Only a small percentage of these professionals specialise in food photography. Such jobs are [Q20(typically)] freelance-based and highly competitive. Some photographers join the International Association of Culinary Professionals - Food Photographer and Stylist Division in hopes of landing more jobs.
zh: 你有没有见过牛排、沙拉或一片草莓短蛋糕的照片，让你垂涎三尺？像这样的画面都是由注重细节的专业食品摄影师创作的。这些艺术家通过别出心裁的创意思考，让他们的受众在没有食物实际呈现、味道、香气和质感的情况下，也对某道菜产生渴望。食品摄影师致力于为杂志、菜单、食谱和其他类型的媒体创作并拍摄下这些美丽动人的食物图像。他们必须在使用数码相机和相关技术方面拥有极好的知识和丰富经验。
他们与食品造型师密切合作，让食物看起来尽可能美味可口和吸引人。新加坡大约雇用了1000名摄影师。这些专业人士中只有一小部分人专门从事食品摄影。这类工作通常是自由职业性质的，而且竞争异常激烈。一些摄影师加入了国际烹饪专业人士协会——食品摄影师与造型师分会，希望能获得更多的录用机会。

21.stem_plain: According to the visual text, the main purpose is to ________.

21.note: Prototype paper — replace stems, passages, and teaching copy when content is ready.

29.concept: 介词搭配（动介固定搭配）
29.note: ‘clouds the water surface’ 或者是与修饰语连用。结合语境‘晨雾笼罩了麦里芝蓄水池的水面’，此处名词作动词 clouds 意为笼罩，其前面常有定冠词 the 修饰整个名词短语，或者是与整个水面有关。检查选项，由于横线处在 clouds 后面，水面 water surface 前面，特指该蓄水池的水面，应用定冠词 the。

30.concept: 介词用法（表示方向或归属）
30.note: ‘A gateway to Singapore’s nature reserves’，gateway 后常接介词 to，表示‘通往……的门户’。

31.concept: 介词用法（表示对象或目的）
31.note: ‘a popular spot for nature lovers...’，介词 for 引入对象，意为‘深受大自然爱好者欢迎的去处’。

32.concept: 动词时态与语态（一般过去时被动语态）
32.note: ‘the MacRitchie Reservoir Park was opened in 1868’，句子主语是公园单数，且有明确的过去时间状语 in 1868，故使用一般过去时单数被动语态，选 was。

33.concept: 情态动词（表示可能性或允许）
33.note: ‘Visitors can take a morning or evening stroll...’，情态动词 can 在此表示具备某种可能或条件，意为‘游客们可以在水边散步’。

34.concept: 并列连词/副词（并列顺承）
34.note: ‘admire the beauty and serenity...’，连词 and 连接两个并列的抽象名词名词 beauty（美景）与 serenity（宁静）。

35.concept: 动词时态与主谓一致（一般现在时）
35.note: ‘The MacRitchie Reservoir Park is also a popular venue...’，本句是在陈述一个客观事实，主语为单数名词，全篇用一般现在时，故系动词选 is。

36.concept: 连词用法（时间/伴随状语从句）
36.note: ‘while embracing the wonders...’ 连词 while 在此引导省略主语的状语从句（分词结构伴随），意为‘同时去拥抱我们本土生物多样性的奇迹’。

cloze: The gentle splash of a lone kayaker scudding across the water breaks the silence. A few metres away, a family of otters dives into the water as the early morning mist clouds [Q29] water surface of the MacRitchie Reservoir.

A gateway [Q30] Singapore's nature reserves, the MacRitchie Reservoir Park is a popular spot [Q31] nature lovers and exercise enthusiasts. Surrounded by lush forest, the MacRitchie Reservoir Park [Q32] opened in 1868 and is the oldest of Singapore's seventeen reservoirs. Visitors [Q33] take a morning or evening stroll along the water's edge to admire the beauty [Q34] serenity of the reservoir.

The MacRitchie Reservoir Park [Q35] also a popular venue for cross-country events. The carefully planned routes allow participants to run through designated trails [Q36] embracing the wonders of our native biodiversity.
zh: 独行皮划艇划过水面的轻柔拍击声打破了宁静。几米开外，一个水獭家族跃入水中，此时清晨的薄雾正笼罩着麦里芝蓄水池的水面。
作为通往新加坡自然保护区的门户，麦里芝蓄水池公园是大自然爱好者和健身爱好者的热门去处。麦里芝蓄水池公园四周环绕着茂密的森林，它于1868年开放，是新加坡17个蓄水池中最古老的一个。游客们可以在水边清晨或傍晚漫步，欣赏蓄水池的美丽与宁静。
麦里芝蓄水池公园也是越野赛的热门举办地。精心规划的路线允许参赛者穿过指定的步道，同时去亲身拥抱我们本土生物多样性的奇迹。

39.note: 冠词错误：此处指“一份时间表”，应用不定冠词 a 代替定冠词 the。

40.note: 拼写错误：正确拼写为 consistent（形容词，意为始终如一的、连续的）。

41.note: 拼写错误：正确拼写为 accomplished（形容词/过去分词，意为完成的）。

42.note: 拼写错误：正确拼写为 overwhelming（形容词，意为令人不知所措的）。

cloze: One of the most practical ways of getting important tasks done is by doing them a little at a time. Create [Q39(the)] timetable by setting aside the same time each day or blocking out specific periods in your daily schedule to complete a task or a piece of work.

The key is to be [Q40(consitant)] and slowly foster a habit. Once this happens, you will get used to doing it and a part of the task will be [Q41(acompleashed)] each day. Let's use writing a book as an example. At first it will seem like an [Q42(overwelming)] task. But if you set your goal to writing one page a day, even if you take a break during the weekends, you will have [Q43(complete)] a 260-page book at the end of the year. We can also compare this [Q44(technik)] to building a brick house. The individual bricks can be small and [Q45(lay)] them

one at a time can be painfully slow. However, when those bricks are constantly placed on top of each other, a strong wall or pillar is created. Therefore, [Q46(unless)] we plan our time well, it not only helps us to get more work done but also [Q47(developing)] self-discipline. This ultimately helps us to overcome our habit of [Q48(procratinasion)].

Successful time management is the result of hard work done daily through the [Q49(affactive)] use of time. If you are achieving your daily goals, you are living [Q50(productive)]. Such daily achievements are the building blocks of a successful life.
zh: 完成重要任务最实用的方法之一就是一点一点地去执行。你可以通过每天固定抽出相同的时间，或者在日常日程中留出特定的时间段来完成一项任务或一件工作，以此来制定一份时间表。
关键在于保持始终如一，并慢慢培养出一种习惯。一旦习惯成自然，你就会习惯于去执行它，而且每天都会完成该任务的一部分。让我们以写一本书为例：刚开始时它看起来可能是一项艰巨而令人不知所措的任务。但如果你把目标设定为每天写一页，即使你在周末休息，到年底你也将会完成一本260页的书。我们也可以把这种技巧比作建造砖房。单块的砖头可能很小，而且把它们
一块接一块地砌上去可能会慢得令人痛苦。然而，当这些砖块不断地叠加在彼此之上时，一堵坚固的墙壁或柱子就建立起来了。因此，如果我们好好规划我们的时间，它不仅能帮助我们完成更多的工作，还能培养我们的自律能力。这最终会帮助我们克服拖延的习惯。
成功的的时间管理是每天通过高效利用时间并付出艰苦努力的结果。如果你正在实现你的每日目标，那么你的生活就过得很有效率。而这些日常的成就，正是一个成功人生的基石。

cloze: Thousands of edible water bottles were handed out at the 2019 London Marathon in an attempt to reduce plastic waste.

Runners generally prefer plastic water bottles [Q51] paper cups of water as they are more convenient to drink from when running. Therefore, at the [Q52] of a marathon, a sea of plastic waste is usually found as thirsty runners attempt to stay hydrated [Q53] drinking from, then discarding, bottles of water as they run.

However, this time, [Q54] of the event had arranged for all runners to be handed edible pods filled with a sports drink as they [Q55] along the grueling 42-km route while trying to clock the fastest time.

These 'Ooho!' pods, designed by a London-based company, were made using a common ingredient [Q56] many may be familiar with - seaweed. The pods could be bitten to release the liquid inside and the outer covering could also be swallowed. However, if runners [Q57] not to swallow the outer covering, they could throw [Q58] on the ground. This was perfectly fine as the pods were designed to break apart within four to six weeks - a relatively short time period. In [Q59], it would take 450 years for plastic bottles to disintegrate.

"The marathon is just a stepping stone. We are hoping that the 'Ooho!' pods can be used [Q60] a much larger scale in the future [Q61] as during music festivals," said Rodrigo Gonzalez, one of the company's founders.
[Q62] these efforts, the 2019 marathon was still not entirely plastic-free [Q63] water bottles were available in shops along the route.

With the goal of reducing unnecessary plastic waste, the main sponsors of the event had also guaranteed that all water bottles [Q64] during the marathon would be made partly from recycled plastic. In addition, all these plastic bottles that the runners had used would be [Q65] up and recycled.
All in all, this 'Ooho!' pod campaign had helped to reduce the use of hundreds of thousands of plastic bottles.
zh: 2019年伦敦马拉松赛上分发了数千个可食用“水瓶”，试图以此减少塑料垃圾。
跑步者通常更喜欢塑料水瓶，而不是纸杯装的水，因为在跑步时从塑料瓶里喝水更方便。因此，在马拉松结束时，通常会发现一片塑料垃圾的汪洋，因为口渴的跑者们试图通过从水瓶中饮水然后将其丢弃的方式来保持水分。
然而，这一次，活动的赞助商已经安排在所有跑者沿着艰难的42公里路线奔跑时，向他们分发装有运动饮料的可食用荚舱，以便他们争取跑出最快时间。
这些名为“Ooho!”的荚舱由一家总部位于伦敦的公司设计，是用一种许多人可能都很熟悉的常见原料——海藻制成的。咬开这些荚舱就能释放出里面的液体，外层包装壳也可以被吞下。然而，如果跑者选择不吞下外层包装壳，他们也可以把它们扔在地上。这完全没有问题，因为这些荚舱被设计在四到六周内分解——这是一个相对较短的时间周期。相比之下，塑料瓶需要450年才能降解。
“马拉松只是一个跳板。我们希望‘Ooho!’荚舱在未来可以应用在更大的规模上，比如在音乐节期间，”该公司创始人之一罗德里戈·冈萨雷斯说。
尽管付出了这些努力，2019年的马拉松依然未能完全摆脱塑料，因为沿途的商店里仍有出售瓶装水。
本着减少不必要塑料垃圾的目标，活动的主要赞助商还保证，在马拉松期间分发的所有水瓶都将部分由再生塑料制成。此外，跑者们使用过的所有这些塑料瓶都将被集中收集起来并进行回收利用。
总而言之，这次“Ooho!”荚舱活动帮助减少了数十万个塑料瓶的使用。

paragraphs.1: 这条河干涸了。克拉拉已经不记得上一次有水流过是什么时候了。很久没有下雨，储水箱也快干了。她必须再次订购水，而这需要花钱，可她并没有多少钱。他们还能坚持多久？自从她的哥哥斯科特决定不再和农场有任何关系并离开后，她就一直在苦苦挣扎。恢复她的父母年纪太大，无法干农活，而且很难雇到帮手。由于城市的工薪更高，人们纷纷离开农村。克拉拉束手无策。
paragraphs.8: 接ucionales一个星期，克拉拉开车去镇上办些杂事。在回来的路上，她看到路边有一个广告牌，上面写着提供住宿和早餐（民宿）。她知道这就是解决办法。她读过很多关于生活在城市里的人渴望体验乡村生活的故事。他们家可以以合理的价格在农场提供住宿和餐饮。“如果客人热衷于体验农活，也许我还可以收取额外的费用，”她想道。现在她唯一要做的就是说服她的父母。
paragraphs.15: “不行，”父亲反对道。“这是一个正在运转的农场，不是给那些连马和牛都分不清的人准备的农场住宿。”
paragraphs.17: “考虑到我们农场上根本没有牛，那应该不是问题，”克拉拉说。“爸爸，我真的觉得我们别无选择。一半的绵羊已经死了，剩下的也活不了多久。如果我们有了付费的客人，我们就可以买更多的饲料，并运进更多的水。”
paragraphs.21: “但是家里有陌生人走动，就不会有家的感觉了，”父亲说。
paragraphs.22: “不，会有家的感觉。这仍然是我们的房子，你盖的那些房间也依然会在这里，”克拉拉向他保证。
paragraphs.24: “约翰，如果我们不这样做，我们可能无法让这个地方再维持多久了，”克拉拉的妈妈安娜说。
paragraphs.26: “而且这只会是在周末，”克拉拉恳求道。
paragraphs.27: 约翰点了点头。“只有一个条件——如果客人把我的农场搞得一团糟，这必须立即停止。”
paragraphs.29: 于是，他们三个人为迎接客人准备了房子。克拉拉获得了所有的批准并投放了第一则广告。广告刊登的那天，他们收到了三份预订。然后，克拉拉开始为他们的决定感到担心。万一客人们蛮不讲理、要求苛刻，而且食物不够好怎么办？克拉拉已经尽其所能做好了准备。她只希望第一批客人能和蔼可亲。
paragraphs.35: 不久，第一批来自城市的客人到了。他们以前从未住过农场房屋。只要有一只袋鼠跳过房子前方的围场，就足以让他们的周末变得终生难忘。客人们被这种动物深深吸引，高兴地回家了。
paragraphs.39: 接下来的客人则是另外一回事了。没有什么事情能让他们满意。风景不够优美。他们没有看到足够多的动物。床太硬了。饭菜分量不够，而且他们对农场如何运转毫无兴趣。然而最终，他们还是付了钱，而这正是克拉拉所需要的。
